Suppose $C$ is a self-dual completely regular linear code over a finite field with covering radius $\rho=3$ and minimum distance $d \geq 3$. What is the block length of $C$?

In the theory of fibered surfaces, the slope of a relatively minimal fibration $f \colon S \to B$ over a smooth curve $B$ with general fiber of genus $g$ is defined as the ratio $\lambda(f) = K_{S/B}^2 / \deg(f_*\omega_{S/B})$. What is the exact supremum of the slopes of all such fibrations with general fiber of genus $g \geq 3$ that possess a trivial vertical fundamental group?

A left brace in which every subbrace is an ideal is called a Dedekind left brace. What is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that every multipermutational Dedekind left brace whose additive group is an elementary abelian $p$-group is guaranteed to be multipermutational of level $k$?
Let $r(S_4)$ be the complex representation ring of the symmetric group $S_4$. Up to equivalence, how many irreducible based modules of rank up to 5 over $r(S_4)$ are there?

The competition-common enemy graph (CCE graph) of a digraph $D$ is the undirected graph with vertex set $V(D)$ where distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent if and only if $u$ and $v$ have a common predator (a vertex with directed edges to both $u$ and $v$) and a common prey (a vertex with directed edges from both $u$ and $v$) in $D$. A digraph is called an $\langle i,j \rangle$ digraph if each vertex has indegree at most $i$ and outdegree at most $j$. What is the maximum integer $k$ such that if the CCE graph of an acyclic $\langle 2,2 \rangle$ digraph has at most $k$ components, the CCE graph is guaranteed to be an interval graph?

Consider the self-dual $U(1)$-Yang-Mills-Higgs functional in $\mathbb{R}^n$ given by
$$ E_1(u,
abla;B_R):=\int_{B_R}\left[|
abla u|^2+ rac{(1-|u|^2)^2}{4}+|F_
abla|^2ight] $$
It is proven that entire critical points $(u,
abla)$ with $u(0)=0$ and energy bounded by $(2\pi+	au(n)) \omega_{n-2}R^{n-2}$ for all $R>0$ (where $	au(n)>0$ is a small dimensional constant) have a unique blow-down. Furthermore, it is proven that such critical points are necessarily two-dimensional in ambient dimensions $2\leq n\leq k$, or in any dimension $n\ge2$ if one additionally assumes that $(u,
abla)$ is a local minimizer. What is the precise integer value of $k$?

Consider the set of all connected simple graphs $\Gamma$ of valency at least 3 that admit a finite almost simple arc-transitive group $X$ of automorphisms such that $\Gamma$ has a 2-cell embedding as a map on a closed surface admitting a core-free arc-transitive subgroup $G$ of $X$. Ignoring the infinite family of graphs corresponding to the case where $X$ and $G$ have socles $A_n$ and $A_{n-1}$ respectively, all other such graphs $\Gamma$ belong to exactly two infinite families (the complete graphs $K_n$ with $n$ a prime power, and the Johnson graphs $J(n,2)$ with $n-1$ a prime power) along with exactly $k$ further exceptional graphs. What is the value of $k$?
It has been proven that a cubic graph embedded in the projective plane is 3-edge-colorable if and only if its dual multigraph is $k$-vertex-colorable. What is the value of the integer $k$?

Given a graph $G$, let $\chi(G)$ and $\omega(G)$ respectively denote its chromatic number and clique number. For a class of graphs $\mathcal{G}$, the smallest $\chi$-binding function $f^*$ is defined as $f^*(x) := \max\{\chi(G) \mid G \in \mathcal{G} \text{ and } \omega(G)=x\}$. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the class of $(P_2+P_3, \text{gem})$-free graphs, where $P_2+P_3$ is the disjoint union of a path on $2$ vertices and a path on $3$ vertices, and a gem graph is formed by adding a universal vertex to a path on $4$ vertices. What is the exact value of $f^*(20)$?

Consider colorings of the set of all 2-element subsets of the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ using an arbitrary finite number of colors. Let $k$ be the minimum integer such that for every such coloring, there is guaranteed to be a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ homeomorphic to the rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$ where the 2-element subsets of $S$ take on at most $k$ colors. What is the value of $k$?

For a non-decreasing sequence $S=(s_1,s_2,\ldots)$ of positive integers, an $S$-packing $\ell$-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of its vertex set into subsets $X_1,\ldots, X_\ell$, such that vertices in $X_i$ are pairwise at distance greater than $s_i$ (where distance refers to the shortest path length in $G$) for every $i\in\{1,\ldots,\ell\}$. The $S$-packing chromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\chi_S(G)$, is the minimum $\ell$ for which $G$ admits an $S$-packing $\ell$-coloring. Let $G(\mathbb{Z},\{k,t\})$ be the distance graph whose vertex set is $\mathbb{Z}$, with two vertices $x,y\in \mathbb{Z}$ adjacent whenever $|x-y|\in\{k,t\}$. For positive integers $k$ and $t$ such that $k+t$ is odd, what is the value of $\chi_S(G(\mathbb{Z},\{k,t\}))$ when $S=(1,1,2,2,2,\ldots)$?

Let $\mathfrak{h}$ be the 3-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero. Let $H_E(\mathfrak{h})$ denote the even-degree part of the cohomology associated to the cotangent bundle of the corresponding Heisenberg Lie group, given by $H_E(\mathfrak{h}) = \bigoplus_{i+j \text{ even}} H^i(\mathfrak{h}, \bigwedge^j \mathfrak{h})$. What is the dimension of $H_E(\mathfrak{h})$ as a vector space?

Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group of all permutations on $\{1,\dots,n\}$. The Kendall $\tau$-distance between two permutations $\pi, \sigma \in S_n$ is the number of pairs $(i,j)$ such that $1 \le i < j \le n$ and the relative order of $\pi(i)$ and $\pi(j)$ disagrees with the relative order of $\sigma(i)$ and $\sigma(j)$. Let $P(n, d)$ denote the maximum size of a permutation code of length $n$ with minimum Kendall $\tau$-distance $d$, which is defined as the maximum cardinality of a subset $C \subseteq S_n$ such that the Kendall $\tau$-distance between any two distinct elements in $C$ is at least $d$. For all integers $n \geq 6$ and all integers $d$ satisfying $\frac{3}{5}\binom{n}{2} < d \leq \frac{2}{3}\binom{n}{2}$, what is the exact value of $P(n, d)$?
A conjecture of Várilly-Alvarado states that an $n \times n$ magic square of squares exists for all integers $n \geq n_0$. What is the value of the integer $n_0$?

A regular partial difference set with parameters $(v,k,\lambda,\mu)$ in a group $G$ of order $v$ is a subset $D \subseteq G$ of size $k$, with the identity $1_G \notin D$ and $D=D^{-1}$, such that the expressions $d_1 d_2^{-1}$ for $d_1,d_2 \in D$ with $d_1 \neq d_2$ represent each non-identity element of $D$ exactly $\lambda$ times and each non-identity element of $G \setminus D$ exactly $\mu$ times. Up to isomorphism, there are 267 groups of order 64. In exactly how many of these non-isomorphic groups of order 64 does there exist a regular partial difference set with parameters $(64, 18, 2, 6)$?

Let $p_k(n)$ denote the number of $k$-regular partitions of $n$, and let $p(n)$ denote the usual partition function. For any integer $k \ge 2$, define the exception sets $E_k = \{(a,b) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : 1 < a \le b, p_k(a) p_k(b) = p_k(a+b)\}$ and $F_k = \{(a,b) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : 1 < a \le b, p_k(a) p_k(b) < p_k(a+b)\}$. Similarly, let $E_\infty$ and $F_\infty$ denote the corresponding exception sets for the usual partition function $p(n)$. What is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $E_k = E_\infty$ and $F_k = F_\infty$?

Let $O$ be a point distinct from the center inside a circular billiard table. Consider the family of rays emanating from $O$ and let $\Gamma_n$ be the caustic of the reflected family of rays after $n$ reflections off the circle, for any positive integer $n$. What is the exact number of ordinary cusps of the caustic $\Gamma_n$?

Gravitational instantons of type ALH and ALH* can be constructed via a gluing procedure such that, away from a finite set of exceptional points, the metric collapses with codimension-1 bounded curvature to a quotient of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by a group action generated by $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and a lattice of rank two. In this limit, the exceptional points are modelled either on the Atiyah-Hitchin manifold or on the Taub-NUT metric. How many exceptional points are modelled on the Atiyah-Hitchin manifold in this geometry?

Let $Z(G)$ and $\gamma(G)$ denote the zero forcing number and the domination number of a graph $G$, respectively. What is the smallest integer $c$ such that the inequality $Z(G) \le \gamma(G) + c$ holds for all connected, cubic, claw-free graphs $G$?

Two players play a game by alternately splitting a surface of a compact $2$-manifold along a simple closed curve that is not null-homotopic and attaching disks to the resulting boundary; the last player who can move wins. Let $G(S)$ denote the nim-value of the game played on a surface $S$, and let $S_g$ denote the connected orientable surface of genus $g$. What is the value of $G(S_{2024})$?

Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $J(C)$ be its Jacobian. Let $G$ be a finite group acting on $C$. Consider the induced action of $G$ on $J(C)$. What is the smallest integer $g_0$ such that for all $g \ge g_0$, the quotient variety $J(C)/G$ is never uniruled, given that there exist examples of curves of genus $g_0-1$ and $g_0-2$ for which such a quotient is uniruled?
Let $T$ be a staircase rank-one transformation with cut parameters $r_j \sim j^d$, where $0 < d < 0.2$. What is the multiplicity of the homogeneous spectrum of the Cartesian product $T \otimes T$?

A graph $G=(V,E)$ is a $k$-leaf power if there is a tree $T$ whose leaves are the vertices of $G$ with the property that a pair of leaves $u$ and $v$ induce an edge in $G$ if and only if they are distance at most $k$ apart in $T$. For some values of $k$, there exists a finite set $F_k$ of graphs such that the class of $k$-leaf power graphs is characterized as the set of strongly chordal graphs that do not contain any graph in $F_k$ as an induced subgraph. What is the smallest positive integer $k$ for which no such finite set $F_k$ exists?

It is a theorem that whenever a direct sum of sufficiently many copies of the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is countably coloured, there are arbitrarily large finite sets $X$ whose sumsets $X+X$ are monochromatic. Conversely, if an abelian group $G$ has no elements of order $n$, then there exists a countable colouring of $G$ such that there is no monochromatic sumset $X+X$ for any subset $X \subseteq G$ of size $2$. What is the integer $n$?

Consider the Ising Curie-Weiss model on the complete graph, where the spin vector is constrained under a given $\ell^{p}$ norm for $p>0$. For $p>2$, there exists a critical inverse temperature $\beta_{c}(p)$ such that for $\beta<\beta_{c}(p)$, the magnetization is concentrated at zero and satisfies a Gaussian Central Limit Theorem, whereas for $\beta>\beta_{c}(p)$ the magnetization is concentrated at $\pm m_\ast$ for some $m_\ast>0$. What is the exact value of $\lim_{p\to\infty}\beta_{c}(p)$?

For a compact set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, let the Hausdorff distance from $A$ to its convex hull $\text{conv}(A)$ be defined by $d(A) := \sup_{a \in \text{conv}(A)} \inf_{x \in A} |x - a|$, where $|x|$ is the standard Euclidean norm. The Dyn-Farkhi conjecture states that the function $d^2$ is subadditive on compact sets, meaning $d(A+B)^2 \leq d(A)^2 + d(B)^2$ for all compact sets $A, B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. What is the largest integer dimension $n$ for which this conjecture holds true?

In the Newtonian planar three-body problem, a syzygy is defined as a configuration where the positions of the three bodies are collinear, and a velocity syzygy is a configuration where their velocities are parallel. For a collision-free solution with negative total energy and zero angular momentum, what is the smallest integer $n$ such that every interval of time containing $n$ consecutive syzygies is guaranteed to also contain at least one velocity syzygy?

Let $M$ be the complement in $S^3$ of a $2$-bridge link $L$ with two components. The Thurston norm is a seminorm on $H_2(M, \partial M ; \mathbb{R}) \cong \mathbb{R}^2$, whose unit ball is a convex polygon. What is the maximum possible number of edges (i.e., $1$-dimensional faces) that this unit ball can have?

Consider the set of all 30 MacMahon colored cubes, where each face is painted with one of six colors and every color appears on at least one face. A puzzle involves selecting a collection of eight distinct MacMahon cubes to build a $2\times 2\times 2$ model whose external coloring matches a specified target MacMahon cube, without the restriction that touching interior faces must be the same color. Over all possible collections of eight distinct MacMahon cubes, what is the maximum number of distinct target MacMahon cubes that can be built from a single collection of eight cubes?

Consider a sequence of graphs $G_n$ where the vertex set consists of all composite integers $c$ such that $4 \leq c \leq n$. Two distinct vertices in $G_n$ are connected by an undirected edge if and only if they are relatively prime. It is known that $G_n$ is a connected graph for all $n \geq 49$. What is the exact diameter (the maximum shortest path length between any pair of vertices) of the graph $G_n$ for any $n \geq 289$?

Consider the space $\mathbb{R}^n$ equipped with the $\ell_\infty$-norm. Two vectors $x, y$ in this space form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if $\|x+y\| = \|x\| + \|y\|$. A linear map $T: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is called a TEA preserver if for every TEA pair $x, y$, the vectors $T(x), T(y)$ also form a TEA pair. It has been proven that for exactly one integer dimension $n \ge 1$, there exist nonzero TEA preservers on $\mathbb{R}^n$ that are not a scalar multiple of an $\ell_\infty$-norm isometry. What is this exceptional dimension $n$?

The left and right diameters of a monoid are topological invariants defined in terms of suprema of lengths of derivation sequences with respect to finite generating sets for the universal left or right congruences. Let $C$ be an infinite chain (totally ordered set), and let $\operatorname{End}(C)$ be the endomorphism monoid of $C$ consisting of all order-preserving maps from $C$ to itself. What is the left diameter of $\operatorname{End}(C)$?

Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the class of all finite soluble groups $G$ with the property that every commutator in $G$ has prime power order. What is the maximum number of distinct prime factors that the order of the commutator subgroup $G'$ can have for a group $G \in \mathcal{G}$?
In the context of tropical geometry, what is the Krull dimension of the rational function semifield of a tropical curve that does not consist of only a single point?

Two Fano planes defined on the same set of 7 points are said to be orthogonal if they share no lines. Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be any two orthogonal Fano planes on the same set of 7 points. What is the order of their common automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(F_1) \cap \operatorname{Aut}(F_2)$?

For a simple graph $G$, an edge coloring of $G$ is called an improper interval edge coloring if for every $v\in V(G)$ the colors (which are integers) of the edges incident with $v$ form an integral interval. The interval coloring impropriety of $G$, denoted by $\mu_{int}(G)$, is the smallest integer $k$ such that $G$ has an improper interval edge coloring where at most $k$ edges of $G$ with a common endpoint have the same color. What is the maximum possible value of $\mu_{int}(G)$ over all simple outerplanar graphs $G$?

Let $R$ be a p.q.-Baer $*$-ring. It is a known theorem that the complement of the strong zero-divisor graph of $R$ is connected if and only if the $*$-ring $R$ contains at least $n$ central projections. What is the value of the integer $n$?

An algebra over the complex numbers is called shift associative if it satisfies the identity $(xy)z=y(zx)$ for all elements $x, y, z$. What is the smallest possible dimension of a complex shift associative algebra that is not associative?

Let $X$ be a smooth, complex Fano 4-fold admitting a rational contraction onto a 3-fold (i.e., a rational map $X \dashrightarrow Y$ that factors as a sequence of flips $X \dashrightarrow X'$ followed by a surjective morphism $X' \to Y$ with connected fibers, where $Y$ is a normal projective variety of dimension 3). Suppose $X$ is not isomorphic to a product of del Pezzo surfaces. What is the maximum possible value of the Picard number $\rho(X)$?

In quantum information theory, the quantum Chernoff exponent characterizes the asymptotic error probability in hypothesis testing. Consider the generalized task of discriminating among an arbitrary, a priori known library of reflective targets. In the limit of low transmitter brightness, high loss, and high thermal background, let $E_{\mathrm{QI}}$ be the Chernoff exponent of the error probability when using a Gaussian-state entangled quantum illumination (QI) probe, and let $E_{\mathrm{CI}}$ be the Chernoff exponent when using classical coherent-state illumination (CI) of the same brightness. What is the asymptotic value of the ratio $\frac{E_{\mathrm{QI}}}{E_{\mathrm{CI}}}$?

Every polygon with $n$ vertices in the complex projective plane is naturally associated with its adjoint curve of degree $n-3$. In particular, the adjoint of a heptagon ($n=7$) is a plane quartic. What is the exact number of distinct complex heptagons, up to the action of the dihedral group on the labels of the lines, that have a general plane quartic as their adjoint?

Let $X$ be a projective hyperkähler manifold of K3$^{[n]}$-type with $n \geq 2$. What is the minimum integer $k$ such that every such manifold $X$ with Picard number $\rho(X) \geq k$ is guaranteed to be isomorphic to a moduli space of twisted stable sheaves on a K3 surface?

Consider the stationary sonic-subsonic solutions $\rho$ to the one-dimensional unipolar isothermal hydrodynamic model of semiconductors (Euler-Poisson equations) on the spatial interval $(0,1)$ with a sonic boundary. It has been proven that there exists a critical Sobolev exponent $p_0$ such that the solution $\rho$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W^{1,p}(0,1)$ for any $p < p_0$, but $\rho \notin W^{1,p}(0,1)$ for any $p \ge p_0$. What is the exact value of $p_0$?

Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ be a rectangular random matrix whose entries are independent and identically distributed symmetric random variables with tail probability $\mathbb{P}(|x_{ij}|>t)\sim t^{-\alpha}$ for some parameter $\alpha>0$. Consider the asymptotic regime where $N(n)/n\to \mathsf{a}>1$ as $n \to \infty$. Let $\mathfrak{u}$ be the right singular vector corresponding to the smallest singular value of $X$. There is a phase transition in the localization length of $\mathfrak{u}$: there exists a critical value $\alpha_c$ such that for $\alpha < \alpha_c$, the localization length of $\mathfrak{u}$ is $O(n/\log n)$, and for $\alpha > \alpha_c$, the localization length is of order $n$. What is the exact value of $\alpha_c$?

The power graph of a finite group $G$ is the simple undirected graph with vertex set $G$, in which two distinct elements are adjacent if and only if one is an integer power of the other. The oriented diameter of a $2$-edge-connected undirected graph is the minimum diameter among all its strongly connected orientations. For any integer $n > 6$, what is the exact oriented diameter of the power graph of the cyclic group of order $n$?

The extended mapping class group of a surface is defined to be the group of isotopy classes of (not necessarily orientation-preserving) homeomorphisms of the surface. There is exactly one positive integer $n$ such that the extended mapping class group of an $n$-punctured sphere is NOT generated by two elements of finite order. What is this value of $n$?

For an abelian group $G$ and subsets $A \subseteq D \subseteq G$, define $\ell_D(A) := \min \{ |B| : B \subseteq D, \, A \subseteq B+B \}$. For subsets $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$, suppose $\ell_{\mathbb{Q}}(A) = n$. It is known that there is a constant $c$ such that $\ell_{\mathbb{Z}}(A) \le c n$ for all such subsets $A$, and that this constant is optimal in the sense that for any integer $n$, there exist sets $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ with $\ell_{\mathbb{Q}}(A) = n$ and $\ell_{\mathbb{Z}}(A) \ge c n - O(\sqrt{n})$. What is the value of the constant $c$?

Let $R(G,H)$ denote the Ramsey number, defined as the minimum integer $N$ such that every red-blue edge coloring of the complete graph $K_N$ contains either a red subgraph isomorphic to $G$ or a blue subgraph isomorphic to $H$. Let $C_4$ denote the cycle graph on $4$ vertices, and let $K_{1, 27}$ denote the star graph with a central vertex and $27$ leaves. What is the exact value of the Ramsey number $R(C_4, K_{1, 27})$?

It has been proven that for any $\varepsilon > 0$, the $k$-Dimensional Matching problem is hard to approximate within a factor of $\frac{k}{C + \varepsilon}$ for large $k$ unless $\mathsf{NP} \subseteq \mathsf{BPP}$. This lower bound improves upon the previous $\Omega(k/\log k)$ hardness bound and is achieved using an approximation-preserving gadget from $R$-degree bounded $k$-CSPs over alphabet size $R$ to $kR$-Dimensional Matching. What is the value of the integer $C$?

Let $\{F_n\}$ be a sequence of random variables belonging to the second Wiener chaos of an isonormal Gaussian process. It has been established that $\{F_n\}$ converges in distribution to a bilateral-gamma random variable $X \sim BG(\alpha_1, p_1, \alpha_2, p_2)$ satisfying $\alpha_1 \alpha_2 > 1 + |\alpha_1 - \alpha_2|$ and $\frac{p_1}{p_2} = \frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha_2}$, provided that the cumulants of $F_n$ of order $k$ converge to the corresponding cumulants of $X$ for all integers $k$ from $2$ up to a maximum order $m$. What is the value of $m$ required for this convergence?

Consider a uniformly chosen integer-valued 1-Lipschitz function $f$ on a rooted $d$-ary tree of height $n$ (where each non-leaf vertex has exactly $d$ children), satisfying the boundary condition $f(v) = 0$ for all vertices $v$ at distance $n$ from the root. What is the maximum integer $d \ge 2$ such that the weak limit of the distribution of $f$ exists as $n \to \infty$?
For an odd prime $p$, what is the lower central width of the generalised Fabrykowski-Gupta groups and their profinite completions?
In the classification of special 2-flags up to local diffeomorphisms, what is the total number of singularity classes existing in length 5?

Let $\Omega$ be a connected infinite quiver. A theorem states that the category of locally finite-dimensional representations of $\Omega$ has unique representation type (meaning no two indecomposable representations have the same dimension vector) if and only if the underlying graph of $\Omega$ belongs to a certain set $S$ of infinite generalized ADE Dynkin diagrams. Up to isomorphism, what is the cardinality of the set $S$?

The basis number $b(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that $G$ admits a basis for its cycle space in which each edge of $G$ belongs to at most $k$ members of the basis. What is the exact value of $b(G)$ for any non-planar graph $G$ that can be embedded on a surface with Euler characteristic $0$?

A flexible embedded polyhedron is a closed polyhedral surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that can flex continuously without self-intersecting and without changing the shapes of its faces. What is the minimum possible number of vertices that such a polyhedron can have?

Consider sets of $n > 0$ disjoint smooth rational curves on a K3 surface in characteristic 2 such that the sum of the curves is divisible by $2$ in the Picard group. While supersingular K3 surfaces can admit such sets for multiple values of $n$, what is the unique possible value of $n$ if the K3 surface has finite height?

Let $H$ be an $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree $\delta(H) = n/2 - \eta$. Assume that $\eta = \omega(1)$ and $\eta = o(n)$. It has been shown that there is a constant $C$ such that adding $(C+o(1))\eta$ uniformly random edges to $H$ is the sharp perturbed threshold for Hamiltonicity (meaning that adding $(C+o(1))\eta$ edges asymptotically almost surely makes any such graph $H$ Hamiltonian, and this is best possible up to the $o(1)$ error term). What is the value of the constant $C$?

A local antimagic labeling of a graph $F=(V,E)$ is a bijection $f: E \to \{1, \dots, |E|\}$ such that for any two adjacent vertices $u, v \in V$, their induced vertex weights $w(u) \neq w(v)$, where $w(u) = \sum_{e \in E(u)} f(e)$ and $E(u)$ is the set of edges incident to $u$. The local antimagic chromatic number of $F$, denoted $\chi_{la}(F)$, is the minimum number of distinct vertex weights over all local antimagic labelings of $F$. Let $G$ be a 1-regular graph and $H$ be a null graph (a graph with at least one vertex and no edges). What is the exact value of $\chi_{la}(G \vee H)$, where $G \vee H$ denotes the join of $G$ and $H$?

Let $p > 37$ be a prime. What is the tight lower bound on the number of conjugacy classes of non-identity proper subgroups of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(p)$ (which is known to be attained for over a million primes)?

Let $\mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{F}_3)$ be the full quantum flag manifold of $\mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}_3)$. A quantum tangent space and an associated $*$-differential calculus are constructed for this manifold using Lusztig's positive root vectors (with respect to a distinguished reduced decomposition of the longest element of the Weyl group). Within the noncommutative complex geometry of this calculus, what is the exact number of left $\mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}_3)$-covariant almost-complex structures?

In the semidiscrete setting of optimal transport, where the input probability measure is supported on a compact convex set with nonempty interior and has a strictly positive Lipschitz continuous Lebesgue density, and the output measure is finitely discrete, the classical problem is approximated by entropic optimal transport with a regularization parameter $\varepsilon > 0$. The approximation rate of the entropic optimal transport map (in approaching the Brenier map) as $\varepsilon \to 0$ under the dual Lipschitz norm is known to be sharp and given by $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^p)$ up to polylogarithmic factors. What is the value of the exponent $p$?

Let $a_1$ and $a_2$ be fixed positive integers. Let $G$ be the 4-regular circulant graph of prime order $p$ with generators $a_1$ and $a_2$. For sufficiently large $p$, what is the maximum multiplicity of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $G$?

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let $\mathfrak{D}=k[x_0,x_1,x_2]/(2x_0x_2-x_1^2-1)$ be a ring on which $\mathbb{Z}_2$ acts by $x_i\to -x_i$ for $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$. Let $\mathfrak{R}=\mathfrak{D}^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$ be the subring of invariants, and let $X={\rm Spec}(\mathfrak{R})$. What is the minimal integer $n$ such that the surface $X$ admits an algebraic embedding in the affine space $\mathbb{A}_k^n$?

A sequence covering array, denoted $\textsf{SCA}(N;t,v)$, is a set of $N$ permutations of $\{0, \dots, v-1 \}$ such that each sequence of $t$ distinct elements of $\{0, \dots, v-1\}$ reads left to right in at least one permutation. The minimum number of permutations such an array can have is $t!$. Levenshtein conjectured that if an $\textsf{SCA}(t!;t,v)$ exists, then $v \in \{t,t+1\}$. A strength 2 excess coverage array, denoted $\textsf{CA}_{X}(N;2,k,v)$, is an $N \times k$ array with entries from $\{0, \dots, v - 1\}$ such that every ordered pair of distinct symbols appear at least once in each pair of columns and all other pairs appear at least twice. By demonstrating that there is a unique $\textsf{CA}_{X}(42;2,5,6)$ and showing it does not satisfy necessary conditions, a recent theorem established that if an $\textsf{SCA}(7!;7,v)$ exists, then $v \le V$ for a specific integer upper bound $V$. What is the value of $V$?

Permutation clones on a set $A$ are families of permutations of $A^n$ (for $n \ge 1$) that generalize clone theory. It is known that the dual structure to a permutation clone consists of weight mappings $A^k\rightarrow M$ to a commutative monoid $M$. A permutation clone is called *relationally defined* if it corresponds to the case where the dual objects are relations, which is equivalent to the case where $M=\mathbb{B}$. What is the exact number of relationally defined permutation clones on a $2$-element set?

Let $X$ be a nonsingular projective 3-fold of general type with third plurigenus $P_3 \geq 2$, and let $\phi_m$ denote the $m$-th pluricanonical map of $X$. What is the smallest integer $m_0$ such that $\phi_m$ is guaranteed to be birational onto its image for all $m \geq m_0$ on all such 3-folds $X$?
Let $G$ be a directed strongly regular graph with parameters $(v, k, t, \lambda, \mu) = (22, 9, 6, 3, 4)$. What is the maximum possible prime order of an automorphism of $G$?

A set of edges $F$ in a graph $G$ is an edge dominating set if every edge in $G$ is either in $F$ or shares a vertex with an edge in $F$. A graph $G$ is said to be well-edge-dominated if all of its minimal edge dominating sets have the same cardinality. Up to isomorphism, how many 2-connected well-edge-dominated outerplanar graphs are there?

In the study of the thin obstacle problem, the frequencies $\lambda$ of homogeneous solutions are known to exhibit certain gaps. What is the smallest positive integer $a$ such that, in all dimensions, there are no homogeneous solutions to the thin obstacle problem with frequency $\lambda$ belonging to the open interval $(a k, a k + 1)$ for all positive integers $k$?

Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero and $G=\mathrm{GL}(2,F)$. Let $n\geq 2$ be a positive integer and $\widetilde{G}$ be the $n$-fold metaplectic cover of $G$. Let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth representation of a group and $\pi^{\vee}$ be its contragredient. An involutive anti-automorphism $\tau$ of the group is called a dualizing involution if $\pi^\tau \simeq \pi^{\vee}$ for all such $\pi$. By a theorem of Gelfand and Kazhdan, the standard involution on $G$ is a dualizing involution. For exactly which integer value of $n \geq 2$ is any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ a dualizing involution?

The graph coloring game on a graph $G$ is a two-player game played with $k \in \mathbb{N}$ colors. Alice and Bob alternately (starting with Alice) color an uncolored vertex with a color from $\{1,\dots,k\}$ such that no two adjacent vertices receive the same color. Alice wins if eventually all vertices are colored, and Bob wins otherwise. The game chromatic number $\chi_g(G)$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that Alice has a winning strategy on $G$. Let $P_n$ denote the path graph on $n$ vertices, and let $P_4 \times P_n$ denote the Cartesian product of $P_4$ and $P_n$. What is the exact value of $\chi_g(P_4 \times P_n)$ for all integers $n \geq 18$?

Let $S_n$ be the set of all $n \times n$ complex matrices having index at most $1$ (i.e., matrices for which the group inverse $A^\#$ exists). The set $S_n$ is equipped with the sharp partial order, defined for $A, B \in S_n$ by $A \leq_{\#} B$ if and only if $A A^\# = B A^\#$ and $A^\# A = A^\# B$. What is the largest integer $n \ge 1$ such that $S_n$ is a lower semilattice under this partial order?

Let $\Delta(p,q,r)$ denote a compact hyperbolic triangle group. It admits a canonical representation to $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ with discrete image which is unique up to conjugation. The trace field of this representation is given by $K = \mathbb{Q}(\cos(\pi/p), \cos(\pi/q), \cos(\pi/r))$. Exactly how many such compact hyperbolic triangle groups are conjugate to subgroups of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(K)$?

Consider Finsler billiards in a planar domain bounded by an oval (a smooth strictly convex closed curve) and endowed with a projective Finsler metric (a metric whose geodesics are straight segments). A caustic by reflection is defined as the envelope of the oriented lines, representing billiard trajectories, that start at a point inside the billiard and undergo a fixed number of reflections. What is the minimum number of cusps such a caustic is guaranteed to have?

A metric measure space $(Y, \nu)$ is called 1-uniform if it satisfies $\nu(B(y,r)) = r$ for all $y \in Y$ and $r > 0$. Up to isometry and measure-preserving equivalence, how many 1-uniform metric measure spaces exist?

In the affine geometry $\text{AG}(n,2)$, a cap is defined to be a subset of points in which every collection of four points is in general position (i.e., affinely independent). What is the maximum possible size of a cap in $\text{AG}(7,2)$?

In the game of Set, each card is defined by 4 properties, each taking one of 3 possible values (which can be modeled as points in $\mathbb{F}_3^4$). A 'set' consists of 3 distinct cards such that for each property, the values on the 3 cards are either all the same or all mutually distinct (which corresponds to 3 collinear points in $\mathbb{F}_3^4$). What is the absolute maximum possible number of valid sets that can be formed from a subset of exactly 12 distinct cards?

Consider the five-parameter family of planar Kolmogorov systems defined by the differential equations \begin{align*} \dot{y} &= y \left( b_0+ b_1 y z + b_2 y + b_3 z\right), \\ \dot{z} &= z\left( c_0 + b_1 y z + b_2 y + b_3 z\right), \end{align*} where $b_0, b_1, b_2, b_3,$ and $c_0$ are real parameters. What is the exact number of topologically distinct global phase portraits that these systems can exhibit in the Poincaré disc?

A graph is called 1-planar if it can be drawn in the plane such that each edge is crossed by at most one other edge. A graph is called claw-free if it does not contain the complete bipartite graph $K_{1,3}$ as an induced subgraph. What is the maximum possible value for the maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ of a finite claw-free 1-planar graph $G$?
What is the smallest positive integer $n$ for which there exists a pair of mutually unbiased weighing matrices of order $n$ and weight $9$?
Let $X$ be a $\mathbb Q$-factorial canonical Fano $3$-fold of Picard number $1$. What is the optimal upper bound for its degree $(-K_X)^3$?

Consider the contact process on a random graph generated by independent Bernoulli long-range percolation on $\mathbb{Z}$, where the coupling constants satisfy $J_{x,y} \asymp |x-y|^{-\delta}$. A verified conjecture of Can states that the survival/extinction phase transition of the contact process on this graph is guaranteed to be non-trivial whenever $\delta$ is strictly greater than a specific value $\delta_c$. What is this value $\delta_c$?

Let $S$ be a compact, orientable surface with genus $g \ge 1$ or number of boundary components $b \ge 4$. The fine $k$-curve graph of $S$ is defined as the graph whose vertices are simple closed essential curves on $S$, and whose edges connect pairs of curves that intersect in at most $k$ points. The finitary curve graph of $S$ is defined as the direct limit of the fine $k$-curve graphs as $k 	o \infty$. What is the diameter of the finitary curve graph of $S$?

Let $G$ be the Sims-Gewirtz graph. Let $\mathcal{S}(G)$ be the set of all real symmetric matrices $A$ indexed by the vertices of $G$ such that for all $i \neq j$, $A_{i,j} \neq 0$ if and only if vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent in $G$ (with no restrictions placed on the diagonal entries of $A$). What is the minimum possible number of distinct eigenvalues of a matrix $A \in \mathcal{S}(G)$?

Consider the spectral space of conjugacy classes of closed subgroups of $\text{SU}(3)$, which naturally arises in the classification of rational $\text{SU}(3)$-equivariant spectra. This space decomposes into a disjoint union of blocks (connected components), each dominated by a subgroup. How many blocks are there in this decomposition?
How many $5$-regular matchstick graphs exist on the two-dimensional sphere?

Let $f$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables with real coefficients having exactly $n+3$ monomial terms and a Newton polytope of positive volume. Over all $n \ge 1$ and all such polynomials $f$, what is the maximum possible number of connected components of the positive zero set of $f$?

Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a graph. The zero-sum Ramsey number $R(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)$ is the least integer $N$ such that for every edge-coloring $\chi : E(K_N) \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_k$ one can find a copy of $G$ in $K_N$ such that $\sum_{e \in E(G)}{\chi(e)} = 0$ in $\mathbb{Z}_k$. Let $P_7$ be the path graph on 7 vertices and let $K_{1,6}$ be the star graph on 7 vertices. What is the exact value of the sum $R(P_7,\mathbb{Z}_3) + R(K_{1,6},\mathbb{Z}_3)$?

A smooth link of $r$ components is a smooth embedding $\bigsqcup_{i=1}^r S^n \hookrightarrow S^{n+2}$. Such a link is said to be link homotopically trivial if there exists a continuous 1-parameter family of maps to $S^{n+2}$ starting at the link and ending at the trivial link, such that at each time parameter, the images of the $r$ distinct $n$-spheres remain pairwise disjoint. What is the minimum positive integer $n$ such that for every $r \geq 1$, every such link is link homotopically trivial?

In the form of Kontsevich's homological mirror symmetry conjecture establishing an equivalence between the Fukaya category of a projective K3 surface and the derived category of coherent sheaves on its mirror over the field $\mathbb{C}((q))$ of formal Laurent series, what is the Picard rank of this mirror K3 surface?

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite undirected graph. A dichotomous ordinal graph is a graph $G$ along with a partition of its edge set $E$ into two sets, $E_{\text{short}}$ and $E_{\text{long}}$. A geometric realization of a dichotomous ordinal graph $G$ in a metric space $(X,d)$ is a mapping $f: V \to X$ such that for every $e_1=\{u_1,v_1\} \in E_{\text{short}}$ and every $e_2=\{u_2,v_2\} \in E_{\text{long}}$, we have $d(f(u_1), f(v_1)) < d(f(u_2), f(v_2))$. A graph $G$ is called pandichotomous in $X$ if for every possible partition of $E$ into $E_{\text{short}}$ and $E_{\text{long}}$, there exists a geometric realization of the resulting dichotomous ordinal graph in $X$. 

What is the maximum integer $n$ such that the complete bipartite graph $K_{4,n}$ is pandichotomous in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$?

A quasigeodesic is a curve on the surface of a convex polyhedron that has $\le \pi$ surface to each side at every point. A geodesic has exactly $\pi$ to each side at every point. How many simple closed quasigeodesics exist on a cube that are not geodesics, up to symmetries?

Let $G$ be a group. A Cayley digraph on $G$ is called NNN if the Cayley digraph is normal and its automorphism group contains a non-normal regular subgroup isomorphic to $G$. A group is called an NNND-group if there exists an NNN Cayley digraph on the group. What is the smallest order of a dihedral group that is an NNND-group?
Up to isomorphism, what is the exact number of connected oriented graphs whose Hermitian adjacency matrix of the second kind has exactly two distinct eigenvalues?

What is the smallest integer $M$ such that every real number can be expressed as the sum of two real numbers whose partial quotients $a_n$ (for $n \ge 1$) in their nearest integer continued fraction expansions satisfy $|a_n| \le M$?

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces with $\dim(H) \ge 2$. Let $A: H \to K$ be an additive map that preserves orthogonality, meaning that for all $x, y \in H$, $\langle x, y \rangle = 0 \implies \langle A(x), A(y) \rangle = 0$. What is the largest integer $c$ such that the dimension condition $\dim(K) < c \dim(H)$ guarantees that any such mapping $A$ is automatically either complex-linear or conjugate-linear?
What is the real subrank of the $4 \times 4 \times 4$ order-three tensor representing the multiplication of quaternions over $\mathbb{R}$?

Let $p > 7$ be a prime. Consider the sum $S_p$ of the inverses of all Gaussian integers in the set $A = \{n+mi \mid 1 \leq n, m \leq p-1, \gcd(p, n+mi)=1 \text{ in } \mathbb{Z}[i]\}$, where the sum is evaluated in the $p$-adic completion or appropriate local ring. An extension of Wolstenholme's theorem to the ring of Gaussian integers establishes a general congruence of the form $S_p \equiv 0 \pmod{p^k}$ for all such primes $p$. What is the maximum integer $k$ for which this universal congruence holds?

A positive integer $n$ is a friend of $10$ if $n \neq 10$ and $\sigma(n)/n = \sigma(10)/10$, where $\sigma$ denotes the sum of divisors function. Suppose $F = 5^{2a} \cdot Q^2$ is a friend of $10$, where $a$ is an even positive integer and $Q$ is an odd positive integer coprime to $15$. Determine the value of $(\sigma(5^{2a}) + \sigma(Q^2)) \pmod 8$, where the modulo operation returns the least non-negative residue.

Let $\mathcal{Z}_5((\mathbb{Z}_2)^3)$ denote the vector space over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ generated by equivariant unoriented bordism classes of all five-dimensional closed smooth manifolds with effective smooth $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^3$-actions fixing isolated points. What is the dimension $\dim_{\mathbb{Z}_2} \mathcal{Z}_5((\mathbb{Z}_2)^3)$?

The diagonal grade of a formal power series $f(x)$ is defined to be the smallest integer $n \geq 0$ such that $f(x)$ is the diagonal of a rational function in the $n+1$ variables $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$. Let $f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty A_k x^k$ be the ordinary generating function of the Apéry sequence, defined by the coefficients $A_k = \sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j}^2 \binom{k+j}{j}^2$. What is the diagonal grade of $f(x)$?
Up to isomorphism, how many Bol loops of order 27 are there?

Given $N \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathfrak{C}_3(N)$ be the number of pairs of $3\times 3$ matrices $A,B$ with entries in $[-N,N] \cap \mathbb{Z}$ such that $AB = BA$. It is known that there exist positive constants $c_1, c_2$ such that $c_1 N^E \le \mathfrak{C}_3(N) \le c_2 N^E$ for all sufficiently large $N$. What is the exact value of the exponent $E$?

Let $M$ be a closed non-orientable surface. Let $C_2(M)$ and $B_2(M)$ denote the ordered and unordered 2-configuration spaces of $M$, respectively. Let $w_1 \in H^1(B_2(M); \mathbb{F}_2)$ be the first Stiefel-Whitney class of the canonical line bundle associated to the double cover $C_2(M) \to B_2(M)$. The Stiefel-Whitney height of $M$ is defined as the maximum integer $k$ such that $w_1^k \neq 0$ in $H^*(B_2(M); \mathbb{F}_2)$. What is the Stiefel-Whitney height of $M$?

A hole is a chordless cycle with at least four vertices, and it is odd if it has an odd number of vertices. A dart is a graph with vertices $a, b, c, d, e$ and edges $ab, bc, bd, be, cd, de$. Let $G$ be a graph that does not contain a dart or an odd hole as an induced subgraph. Suppose $G$ is not a perfect graph, and $G$ is neither the join nor the co-join of two strictly smaller graphs. What is the independence number $\alpha(G)$ of such a graph $G$?
What is the maximum integer $k$ such that every 2-connected, cubic, planar graph with all faces of size at most $k$ is guaranteed to be Hamiltonian?
Let $\mathfrak{G}$ be the cubic line complex associated with the desmic tetrahedra introduced by G. Humbert. As a $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano threefold, how many nodes does $\mathfrak{G}$ have?

Let $B$ be a left nilpotent skew brace of class $2$ (i.e., $B^3 = 0$) that is of abelian type. What is the smallest integer $n$ such that every such skew brace $B$ is guaranteed to be right nilpotent of class $n$ (i.e., $B^{(n+1)} = 0$)?

Consider solutions $u(t,x) \in L^\infty_t B_{2,1}^{\frac{1}{2}}$ to the Benjamin-Ono equation $\partial_t u - H \partial_x^2 u = -\partial_x(u^2)$ that are localized in a reference frame moving to the right with constant speed $c>0$. It is a known result that if such a solution decays spatially at least as fast as $\langle x-ct\rangle^{-1-\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$, then it must in fact decay as $\langle x-ct\rangle^{-\alpha}$. Assuming $\alpha$ is the sharpest possible exponent, what is the value of $\alpha$?

Let the sequence $a(n)$ be defined by the generating function $\sum_{n=0}^\infty a(n) q^n = \frac{(-q; q)^2_\infty}{(q; q)_\infty}$ for $|q|<1$, where $(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{k=0}^\infty (1-a q^k)$ is the $q$-Pochhammer symbol. There exists a unique integer $b \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ such that $a(7n+b) \equiv 0 \pmod{7}$ for all integers $n \ge 0$. What is the value of $b$?

Let $g_1, g_2$ be loxodromic isometries of the complex hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$. Consider the cyclic subgroup $\Gamma = \langle (g_1, g_2) \rangle$ acting on the complex hyperbolic bidisk $\mathbb{H}^2_{\mathbb{C}} \times \mathbb{H}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$. Suppose the basepoint for the Dirichlet domain is chosen as $(z_1, z_2)$, where $z_1$ and $z_2$ are points lying on the invariant axes of $g_1$ and $g_2$, respectively. How many sides does the Dirichlet domain of $\Gamma$ have?
What is the total number of isomorphism classes of smooth weak Fano toric fourfolds of Picard rank $3$?

Let $S$ be the set of all finite cubic graphs whose adjacency matrix has no eigenvalues in the open interval $(-2,0)$. The set $S$ consists of exactly one infinite family $\mathcal{F}$ (containing exactly one graph on $6n$ vertices for each integer $n \ge 2$) and a finite set $\mathcal{E}$ of exceptional graphs. What is the cardinality $|\mathcal{E}|$?

Let $\Sigma$ be a 2-letter alphabet and let $w$ be an infinite word over $\Sigma$. A finite factor (contiguous subword) $f$ of $w$ is called an \emph{imaged} factor if there exists a non-erasing morphism $m: \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$, distinct from the identity morphism, such that $m(f)$ is also a factor of $w$. What is the maximum integer $N$ such that every infinite binary word $w$ is guaranteed to contain at least $N$ distinct imaged factors?

Let $\omega(n)$ denote the sum of the squares of the coefficients of the polynomial 
$$P_n(x) = \prod_{i=0}^{n-1} \left(1 + x^{2^i+1} + x^{2^{i+1}+1}\right)$$
What is the exact number of decimal digits in the base-10 representation of $\omega(10000)$?

Consider the standard Legendrian Hopf link in the standard contact 3-sphere. Up to compactly supported Hamiltonian isotopy, what is the exact number of oriented embedded exact Lagrangian fillings of this link in the standard symplectic Darboux ball?

Let $X$ be a smooth cubic threefold over the complex numbers. For degree $e \geqslant 5$, what is the exact number of irreducible main components of the Kontsevich moduli space $\overline{M}_{1,0}(X, e)$ of genus one stable maps to $X$?

Let $\ell$ and $n$ be positive integers with $\ell$ prime. In the arithmetic of modular curves, an algebraic point $x$ on a curve defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ is called isolated if it does not belong to any infinite parameterized family of points having the same degree. Over all primes $\ell$ and positive integers $n$, exactly how many $j$-invariants in $\mathbb{Q}$ arise as the image of an isolated point $x \in X_1(\ell^n)$ under the natural map $j: X_1(\ell^n) \rightarrow X_1(1)$?

Let $C(G)$ denote the cycle space of a graph $G$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and let $C_n(G)$ denote the subspace of $C(G)$ spanned by the incidence vectors of the Hamilton cycles of $G$. For a random graph $G \sim \mathbb{G}(n,p)$ with $n$ being an odd integer, there is an integer $k$ such that the minimum degree condition $\delta(G) \geq k$ is asymptotically almost surely necessary and sufficient to ensure that $C_n(G) = C(G)$. What is the value of $k$?

The Pythagoras number $p(F)$ of a field $F$ is defined as the smallest positive integer $n$ such that every sum of squares in $F$ can be written as a sum of at most $n$ squares. What is the maximum value of $p(F)$ among all fields $F$ of transcendence degree $1$ over $\mathbb{Q}$?

Consider the gravitational field equations of scalar field cosmology for a quintessence scalar field $\phi$ in a spatially flat Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) background with an uncoupled dust fluid source. The scalar field potential is $V(\phi) = \alpha(e^{\lambda \phi} + \beta)$, where $\alpha, \beta,$ and $\lambda$ are constants. Painlevé analysis establishes that these cosmological field equations possess the Painlevé property and are integrable strictly when $\lambda^2 > c$. What is the exact numerical value of the constant $c$?
What is the maximum number of lines on a complex non-K3 quartic surface that is not ruled by lines?

Let $d$ be the minimum integer such that for every prime order group $G$ and every finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over the field of rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$, the polynomial invariants of degree at most $d$ separate the orbits. What is the value of $d$?

Let $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{3,n}$ be the moduli space of stable curves of genus $3$ with $n$ marked points. What is the minimum integer $n$ such that $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{3,n}$ is of general type?

Let $G = (V, E)$ be a connected simple graph. For a subset $D \subseteq V$ with $|D| \geq 2$, a $D$-path is a path that includes all vertices in $D$. A collection of such paths is internally disjoint if they intersect only at the vertices of $D$ and share no edges. Let $\pi_G(D)$ denote the maximum number of internally disjoint $D$-paths in $G$. The $k$-path-connectivity is defined as $\pi_k(G) = \min \{ \pi_G(D) \mid D \subseteq V(G),\ |D| = k\}$. Let $AQ_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional augmented cube graph. What is the value of the 3-path-connectivity $\pi_3(AQ_{10})$?

The group of automorphisms of the free group on two generators, $\mathrm{Aut}(F_2)$, is known to act geometrically, in an essentially unique way, on a 2-dimensional CAT(0) space $X$. A Hamiltonian surface in $X$ is defined as a surface in $X$ which visits every vertex and every edge precisely once. Exactly how many Hamiltonian surfaces does $X$ contain?

Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $\rho(G) = \prod_{g \in G} o(g)$ be the product of the orders of all elements in $G$. Let $\rho(G) = p_1^{\alpha_1} p_2^{\alpha_2} \cdots p_k^{\alpha_k}$ be the prime factorization of $\rho(G)$, where the $p_i$ are distinct primes, and define the set of exponents as $\operatorname{Exp}_\rho(G) = \{\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \cdots, \alpha_k\}$. It is known that there is a unique non-abelian finite group $G$ such that $\operatorname{Exp}_\rho(G) = \operatorname{Exp}_\rho(\mathbb{Z}_{2qr})$ for some distinct odd prime numbers $q$ and $r$. What is the order of this group $G$?

Deeley constructed a counterexample to the HK-conjecture (which relates to the stable and unstable groupoids of a Smale space) using an odometer built from a flat manifold of dimension 9 and an expansive self-cover. What is the minimal dimension $d$ of a flat manifold for which there exists an odometer, built from an expansive self-cover of the manifold, that provides a counterexample to the HK-conjecture?

What is the smallest odd prime power $q$ such that every square matrix over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ can be decomposed as a sum $D+M$, where $D$ is a diagonalizable matrix over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $M$ is a matrix over $\mathbb{F}_q$ satisfying $M^2=0$?

A subset of vertices $S$ of a graph $G$ is called a distinguishing set if the only automorphism $g \in \text{Aut}(G)$ that preserves $S$ as a set (i.e., $g(S) = S$) is the identity automorphism. The distinguishing cost of $G$ is the minimal cardinality of a distinguishing set. What is the distinguishing cost of any connected cubic vertex-transitive graph of girth 5 that has exactly two edge orbits?

Let $X$ be a smooth projective hypersurface of dimension at least three that is not a quadric threefold. What is the number of irreducible components of logarithmic type in the space of codimension-one foliations of degree one on $X$?

Consider the multi-dimensional Hegselmann-Krause (HK) dynamics driven by symmetric i.i.d. noise with zero mean, non-zero variance, and bounded norm $\|\xi_i(t)\| \leq \delta \leq \epsilon/2$ in an unbounded continuous space $\mathbb{R}^d$ with confidence threshold $\epsilon$. What is the maximum integer dimension $d$ for which quasi-synchronization is achieved almost surely in finite time for all initial states?

Let $M = (E, \mathcal{I})$ be an arbitrary matroid whose ground set $E$ can be partitioned into $k \ge 2$ bases. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be two arbitrary disjoint subsets of $E$. It is a proven theorem that there always exists a partition of $E$ into $k$ bases $B_1, \dots, B_k$ such that $\max_{1 \le i, j \le k} \left| |B_i \cap S_1| - |B_j \cap S_1| \right| \le 1$. Let $D$ be the minimum integer such that, for every such matroid and every choice of disjoint subsets $S_1, S_2 \subseteq E$, there exists a partition of $E$ into $k$ bases $B_1, \ldots, B_k$ that simultaneously satisfies $\max_{1 \le i, j \le k} \left| |B_i \cap S_1| - |B_j \cap S_1| \right| \le 1$ and $\max_{1 \le i, j \le k} \left| |B_i \cap S_2| - |B_j \cap S_2| \right| \le D$. What is the value of $D$?

The representation number of a graph is the minimum number of copies of each vertex required to represent the graph as a word, such that the letters corresponding to vertices $x$ and $y$ alternate if and only if $xy$ is an edge in the graph. For integers $m \ge 3$ and $n \ge 3$, what is the representation number of the $m \times n$ grid graph?

A negatively curved hyperbolic cone metric on a surface is defined to be rigid if it is uniquely determined by the support of its Liouville current, and flexible otherwise. What is the exact number of mapping class group orbits of equivalence classes of flexible negatively curved hyperbolic cone metrics on the closed orientable surface of genus 2?

Let $G_3$ be the standard Rubik's cube group, defined as the group of permutations of the movable facets of a $3 \times 3 \times 3$ Rubik's cube generated by the 90-degree rotations of its six faces. What is the minimal dimension of a faithful representation of $G_3$ over the complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$?

The Pólya group $\mathrm{Po}(K)$ of a number field $K$ is the subgroup of the ideal class group $\mathrm{Cl}(K)$ of $K$ generated by the classes of all the products of the prime ideals of $K$ with the same norm. The Pólya index of $K$ is defined as the index $[\mathrm{Cl}(K):\mathrm{Po}(K)]$. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), exactly how many imaginary quadratic fields have a Pólya index of $2$?

Let $G$ and $H$ be the non-isomorphic finite $2$-groups recently discovered as counterexamples to the Modular Isomorphism Problem, which have isomorphic group algebras over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ but non-isomorphic group algebras over the $2$-adic integers $\mathbb{Z}_2$. What is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that the group algebras of $G$ and $H$ over the ring $\mathbb{Z}/2^k\mathbb{Z}$ are non-isomorphic?

Let $S_G^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional generalized Sierpiński graph with base graph $G$, and let $\chi_i'(H)$ denote the injective edge chromatic number of a graph $H$. What is the exact value of $\chi_i'(S_{K_3}^n)$ for all $n \ge 3$, where $K_3$ is the complete graph on 3 vertices?

Let $\operatorname{GL}(4, \mathbb{F}_2)$ be the set of all invertible $4 \times 4$ matrices over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_2$. What is the exact number of matrices in $\operatorname{GL}(4, \mathbb{F}_2)$ that cannot be expressed as the Hadamard (entrywise) product $A \circ B$ of two $4 \times 4$ matrices $A$ and $B$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$, where $\operatorname{rank}(A) = 2$ and $\operatorname{rank}(B) = 2$?

A word-representable graph is a graph that can be represented by a word over its vertex set such that two vertices are adjacent if and only if their corresponding letters alternate in the word. Consider the class of graphs whose vertices can be partitioned into two cliques, such that one of the cliques has a size of exactly four and is maximal (i.e., no vertex in the other clique is connected to all vertices of this four-vertex clique). Up to isomorphism, what is the exact number of minimal non-word-representable graphs in this class?

An abstract rotation system of a complete graph $K_n$ assigns to each vertex a cyclic order of its incident edges. A rotation system is defined to be *generalized twisted* if it can be realized as a generalized twisted simple drawing (where any two edges intersect in at most one point, subject to specific geometric constraints). There is a minimal integer $k$ such that for any $n \geq 7$, an abstract rotation system of $K_n$ is generalized twisted if and only if all of its subrotation systems induced by $k$ vertices are generalized twisted. What is the value of $k$?
What is the maximum possible value of the $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano index of a canonical weak Fano $3$-fold?

A covering system of the integers is a finite collection of congruences $x \equiv a_i \pmod{m_i}$ for $1 \le i \le k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one congruence. What is the minimum possible value for the largest modulus $\max_{1 \le i \le k} m_i$ in a covering system where all moduli $m_i$ are distinct and the smallest modulus is exactly $\min_{1 \le i \le k} m_i = 5$?

Consider finite graphs where each edge is colored with one of two colors, 1 or 2. A $k$-majority partition of such a 2-edge-colored graph $G=(V,E)$ is a partition of $V$ into $k$ disjoint subsets such that for each color $c \in \{1,2\}$, every vertex $v \in V$ has at least as many incident edges of color $c$ connecting to vertices outside its own subset as it has incident edges of color $c$ connecting to vertices inside its own subset. What is the minimum integer $k$ such that every 2-edge-colored graph is guaranteed to admit a $k$-majority partition?

The geodesic complexity of a length space $X$ is the minimal integer $k$ such that there is a partition of $X \times X$ into $k+1$ locally compact sets, on each of which there exists a continuous choice of a shortest path connecting any given start and end point. What is the geodesic complexity of the surface of a regular octahedron (equipped with the flat metric)?

Let $X$ be a smooth, complex Fano 4-fold. There exists a minimal integer $N$ such that any smooth, complex Fano 4-fold with Picard number $\rho(X) > N$ is necessarily a product of del Pezzo surfaces. What is the value of $N$?
Up to isomorphism, how many imprimitive finite quaternionic reflection groups of rank two with order $192$ and exactly $22$ reflections exist?

Let $R(G_1, \dots, G_k)$ denote the multicolor Ramsey number, defined as the smallest integer $n$ such that every $k$-coloring of the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $G_i$ in color $i$, where $C_m$ denotes a cycle on $m$ vertices. What is the exact value of the Ramsey number $R(C_3, C_6, C_6)$?
What is the Lorentzian Hausdorff dimension of the sub-Lorentzian Heisenberg group?

In the geometric formulation of the 'angles-only' Initial Orbit Determination problem, the task is to find a planar conic curve in three-dimensional space with a given focal point that intersects a given set of lines of sight. It is known that 5 is the minimal number of lines necessary to yield a finite number of solutions in general position. For a general (non-special) configuration of 5 lines, what is the exact number of complex solutions to this problem?
How many Koszul symmetric set-operads generated by one element of arity $2$ are there up to isomorphism?

Consider a two-stage growth dynamics on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with state space $\{0,1,2\}^{\mathbb{Z}^2}$. Vertices can only irreversibly change states from 0 to 1, and from 1 to 2. A vertex currently in state 0 flips to 1 if it has at least two nearest-neighbors currently in state 1, and a vertex currently in state 1 flips to 2 if it has at least two nearest-neighbors currently in state 2. The initial configuration is drawn from a product measure where vertices are in state 1 with probability $p$, state 2 with probability $q$, and state 0 with probability $1-p-q$. As $p, q \to 0$, there exists a critical exponent $\alpha$ such that if $q$ is asymptotically much larger than $p^{\alpha+o(1)}$, the final density of 0s tends to 1, whereas if $q$ is asymptotically much smaller than $p^{\alpha+o(1)}$, the final density of 2s tends to 1. What is the value of $\alpha$?

Let $P_\infty \boxtimes P_\infty$ denote the infinite diagonal grid (the strong product of two two-way infinite paths). For a sequence of positive integers $S = (a_1, a_2,\ldots)$, the $S$-packing chromatic number of a graph $G$ is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that the vertices can be colored with $k$ colors, where the distance between any two distinct vertices of color $i$ is strictly greater than $a_i$. What is the $S$-packing chromatic number of $P_\infty \boxtimes P_\infty$ for $S = (1,6,6,\ldots)$?

Let $m\colon\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a weak solution of the eikonal equation $|m|=1$ a.e. and $\mathrm{div}\: m =0$. The entropy productions are defined as the distributions $\mu_\Phi=\mathrm{div}\,\Phi(m)$ for a class of smooth vector fields $\Phi$ known as entropies. It is conjectured that if these entropy productions are Radon measures, they must be concentrated on the 1-rectifiable jump set of $m$. This concentration property holds for a large class of entropies under the Besov regularity assumption $m\in B^{1/p}_{p,\infty}$ for any $1\leq p < p_c$, where $p_c$ represents a borderline critical exponent. What is the exact value of this borderline exponent $p_c$?

Let $G$ be the graph consisting of the disjoint union of a cycle graph $C_5$, a cycle graph $C_4$, and a path graph $P_3$. Let $V(G)$ and $E(G)$ denote the vertex and edge sets of $G$, respectively, so that $|V(G)| = 12$. Let $S = K[x_1, \dots, x_{12}]$ be the polynomial ring over a field $K$, where the variables correspond to the vertices of $G$. Let $I_c(G) \subset S$ be the complementary edge ideal of $G$, defined as the ideal generated by all squarefree monomials of degree 10 of the form $\prod_{v \in V(G) \setminus \{i,j\}} x_v$ for each edge $\{i,j\} \in E(G)$. What is the value of $\lim_{k \to \infty} \operatorname{depth} (S/I_c(G)^k)$?

In four-dimensional general $f(\mathbb{Q})$ gravity (symmetric teleparallel gravity), where the action is determined by a general non-linear function $f$ of the non-metricity scalar $\mathbb{Q}$, how many propagating degrees of freedom does the theory possess?

Let $\Lambda$ be an indecomposable finite dimensional hereditary algebra or an indecomposable locally finite hereditary tensor algebra of non-Dynkin type, and let $\Pi$ be the preprojective algebra associated to $\Lambda$. What is the global dimension of $\Pi$?
How many non-trivial Fourier-Mukai partners does a general cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution have?
Let $B^3$ be the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$. What is the Morse index of the free boundary flat Y-cone in $B^3$?
What is the maximum number of distinct limit values (traces) that a Mumford-Shah minimizer in dimension 2 can admit as it approaches the singular set?

The Additive Basis Conjecture for $p=3$ posits that in a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{Z}_3$, the union of any $k$ linear bases is guaranteed to form an additive basis. What is the specific integer value of $k$ stated in this conjecture?

Let $X$ be an arbitrary projective scheme. According to the resolved conjecture of Han, Lee, Moon, and Park, for a sufficiently ample embedding of $X$, its homogeneous ideal is guaranteed to be generated by quadrics of a specific rank $r$. What is the value of $r$?

A proper vertex coloring of a graph $G$ is a strong odd coloring if, for every vertex $v \in V(G)$, each color that is present in the open neighborhood $N(v)$ appears an odd number of times in $N(v)$. The minimum number of colors in a strong odd coloring of $G$ is denoted by $\chi_{so}(G)$. Let $G_d$ be the infinite $d$-dimensional grid graph, whose vertex set is $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and where two vertices are adjacent if and only if their $L_1$ distance is $1$. What is the value of $\chi_{so}(G_d)$ for all integers $d \geq 1$?

Given a digraph $D$ with no loops, the dicoloring graph of $D$, denoted by $\mathcal{D}_k(D)$, is the graph whose vertices are the acyclic $k$-colorings of $D$ and two colorings are adjacent in $\mathcal{D}_k(D)$ if they differ in color on exactly one vertex. For the Paley tournament $\vec{C}_{7}(1,2,4)$, it is proven that the dicoloring graph $\mathcal{D}_k(\vec{C}_{7}(1,2,4))$ is connected for all $k \geq 3$. What is the exact diameter of $\mathcal{D}_k(\vec{C}_{7}(1,2,4))$ for each $k \geq 3$?

Let the sequence $c_1(n)$ be defined by the infinite $q$-series expansion
$$ \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_1(n) q^n = (q^4; q^{10})_\infty^2 (q^6; q^{10})_\infty^2 (q; q^{15})_\infty (q^{14}; q^{15})_\infty $$
where $(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{k=0}^\infty (1 - a q^k)$. There exists a unique integer $r$ such that $0 \le r < 5$ and $c_1(5n+r) = 0$ for all integers $n \ge 0$. What is the value of $r$?

Consider a quantum spin chain with a symmetry $G$ acting via twisted locality-preserving automorphisms, such that its anomaly index in $H^3_\phi(G; U(1))$ is non-trivial. A generalized Lieb-Schultz-Mattis theorem dictates that any Hamiltonian with only two-spin interactions that respects this anomalous symmetry cannot have a unique gapped symmetric ground state, provided the two-spin interactions decay faster than $1/r^\alpha$, where $r$ is the distance between the two interacting spins. What is the value of the threshold exponent $\alpha$?

Let $U \in \mathrm{SU}(2)$ be a single-qubit unitary. Consider the deterministic ancilla-free approximation of $U$ by gate sequences over a Clifford+$G$ gate set, where $p$ is the characteristic factor of the gate set. For Haar-almost every unitary $U$, the minimum $G$-count required to achieve an approximation error at most $\varepsilon$ is asymptotic to $C \log_p(1/\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon \to 0^+$. What is the value of the constant $C$?

Let $m>0$ be a real number. For every $\alpha>0$, let $B_\alpha$ denote the Berezin transform associated to the measure $\mu_m^\alpha$ on the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$, where $\mu_m^\alpha$ has density proportional to $e^{-\alpha|z|^m}$ with respect to the Lebesgue measure and is normalized such that $\mu_m^\alpha(\mathbb C)=1$. Find the unique value of $m$ such that the commutativity relation $B_\alpha B_\beta f = B_\beta B_\alpha f$ holds for all $f\in L^\infty(\mathbb C)$ and all $\alpha, \beta > 0$.

It is a theorem in difference algebra (the proof of which relies on the classification of finite simple groups) that there exists a minimal positive integer $k$ such that for any rational difference equation, if any $k$ distinct solutions are algebraically independent, then any number of distinct solutions to the equation are algebraically independent. What is the value of $k$?

Let $G$ be a group, and let $\omega(G)$ denote the number of orbits of the natural action of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ on $G$. Let $\mathbb{F}$ be an infinite field, and let $UT_n(\mathbb{F})$ denote the group of $n \times n$ unitriangular matrices over $\mathbb{F}$. What is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $\omega(UT_n(\mathbb{F}))$ is infinite?

Fix $g \geq 2$. Let $\mathsf{t}(g)$ be the maximal order of the translation group among all genus-$g$ abelian differentials. Suppose $g$ is such that $\mathsf{t}(g) < 4(g - 1)$ and regular genus-$g$ origamis exist. In this case, it is known that $\mathsf{t}(g) = \frac{2(m + 1)}{m} (g - 1)$ for some integer $m \geq 1$. What is the smallest realizable integer $m > 1$ across all such genera $g$?

Consider the Internal Diffusion Limited Aggregation (IDLA) model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ driven by critical branching random walks whose offspring distribution has positive variance and finite exponential moments. What is the minimum integer dimension $d$ for which this process exhibits a spherical shape theorem?

Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least two vertices, let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, and let $\Delta_2(G)$ denote the maximum number of common neighbors that any two distinct vertices of $G$ have. What is the maximum value of $\chi(G) - \Delta_2(G)$ over all claw-free graphs $G$ with at least two vertices?

What is the minimal dimension $n$ among arithmetic hyperbolic orbifolds of the first type such that there exists an $n$-dimensional orbifold in which every square-rootable Salem number of degree at most 4 over $\mathbb{Q}$ is realized as the exponential of the length of a closed geodesic?

What is the total number of distinct families of smooth complex Fano $4$-folds with Picard number strictly greater than $3$ and Lefschetz defect $\delta(X)=2$ that arise from the Casagrande-Druel construction?

Let $N$ points $U_1,\dots,U_N$ be chosen independently and uniformly inside a triangle $ABC$ of area 1. The boundary of the convex hull of $\{A,B,U_1,\dots,U_N\}$ contains a convex chain from $B$ to $A$ formed by a random number $\mathbf{n}(N)$ of the points $U_i$. Let $n$ and $m$ be positive integers such that $N = n + m$. Conditional on $\mathbf{n}(N)=n$, and assuming $m=\lfloor n\lambda\rfloor$ for a fixed $\lambda>0$, the chain converges in probability (in the Hausdorff topology) to a deterministic limit curve $\mathcal{H}_\lambda$ as $n\to+\infty$. It is established that $\mathcal{H}_\lambda$ is the unique curve maximizing the functional $\mathcal{C} \mapsto \mathsf{Area}(\mathcal{C})^\lambda \mathsf{L}(\mathcal{C})^k$ among all concave curves $\mathcal{C}$ in $ABC$ incident with $A$ and $B$, where $\mathsf{Area}(\mathcal{C})$ is the area associated with $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathsf{L}(\mathcal{C})$ is its affine perimeter. What is the exact integer value of the exponent $k$?

Let $\mu_{GK}$ be the Gauss--Kuzmin measure on $[0,1]$ defined by $\mu_{GK}(I) = \frac{1}{\log 2}\int_I \frac{1}{1+x} dx$. For a string of positive integers $\mathbf{a}=(a_1,\dots,a_n)$, let $I(\mathbf{a})$ denote the set of real numbers in $[0,1)$ whose regular continued fraction expansion begins with the string $\mathbf{a}$. We say $\mathbf{a}$ has a nontrivial symmetry if there exists a string $\mathbf{b}$ that is a permutation of the elements of $\mathbf{a}$, such that $\mathbf{b} \neq \mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b} \neq \overleftarrow{\mathbf{a}}$ (where $\overleftarrow{\mathbf{a}} = (a_n, \dots, a_1)$ is the reverse of $\mathbf{a}$), and $\mu_{GK}(I(\mathbf{a})) = \mu_{GK}(I(\mathbf{b}))$. What is the smallest integer $n \ge 1$ for which there exists a string $\mathbf{a}$ of length $n$ with a nontrivial symmetry?

Let $G$ be a connected Cayley graph for an Abelian group generated by a finite symmetric subset $S$. Suppose its associated Heuberger matrix has exactly $2$ columns and $d$ rows, where $d \geq 5$. Assuming $G$ has no loops, $G$ is not bipartite, and its Heuberger matrix contains no zero rows, what is the chromatic number of $G$?

The spectral gap theorem of Caputo, Liggett, and Richthammer states that on any connected graph equipped with edge weights, the second eigenvalue of the interchange process equals the second eigenvalue of the random walk process. It is a known result that the second eigenspace of the interchange process is uniquely determined by the second eigenvectors of the random walk process on every finite connected weighted graph with at least 3 vertices except for a single cycle graph $C_n$ with uniform edge weights. What is the integer value of $n$?

Let $\Delta_A = d_A^* d_A$ be the covariant Laplacian associated with a smooth $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ connection $A$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$. There is a critical exponent $\gamma$ for the pointwise decay of the curvature $F_A$ that guarantees $\Delta_A$ is a relatively compact perturbation of the flat Laplacian, which implies its essential spectrum is $[0,\infty)$. Specifically, this holds if $|F_A(x)| \le C(1 + |x|)^{-\gamma-\varepsilon}$ for some constant $C>0$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, and the threshold $\gamma$ is sharp because there exist connections with curvature decay $|F_A(x)| \sim |x|^{-\gamma}$ for which this preservation of the essential spectrum fails. What is the exact value of the critical exponent $\gamma$?

Consider the Ising model with an external magnetic field on random tetravalent planar maps. What is the exact value of the critical exponent $\delta$ (characterizing the magnetization at the critical temperature as a function of the external magnetic field) for this model?

An edge-coloring of a graph is called orderable if there exists a linear ordering of its vertices such that the color of each edge is determined solely by its first vertex in the ordering (this definition includes monochromatic colorings). Let $CR(s,t)$ denote the smallest integer $n$ such that every edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_n$ contains an orderable copy of $K_s$ or a rainbow copy of $K_t$. What is the exact value of $CR(6,3)$?

Consider the $p$-dimensional system of Itô type stochastic PDEs:
$$ \partial_t u(t,x) = \partial^2_x u(t,x) + b(u(t,x)) + \sigma(u(t,x)) \xi(t,x) $$
for $(t,x)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{T}$, subject to initial data $u(0) \equiv u_0$ on the one-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}$, where $u_0 \in C^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}; \mathbb{R}^p)$ is fixed and non-random, and $\xi$ denotes a $p$-dimensional space-time white noise. Assume sufficient regularity conditions on $b$ and $\sigma$, and that the set $\{v \in \mathbb{R}^p : \inf_{\|x\|=1} \|\sigma(v)x\| = 0\}$ is polar for $u$. Let $\dim_H$ denote the Hausdorff dimension. For $p \ge 4$, there exists a constant $\alpha$ such that almost surely,
$$ \dim_H u(\{t\}\times F) = \alpha \dim_H F $$
holds simultaneously for all $t>0$ and all compact sets $F \subset \mathbb{T}$. What is the value of $\alpha$?

A standard graded commutative $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ is called cyclotomic if its $h$-polynomial $h_R(t) \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$ has all its roots on the unit circle in the complex plane. A polynomial is defined to be of type CI if it is a product of polynomials of the form $1 + t + \cdots + t^{m-1}$ for positive integers $m$. What is the smallest positive integer $n$ for which there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ whose $h$-polynomial is not of type CI and satisfies $h_R(1) = n$?

Let $V = \{v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4\}$ be an arbitrary set of four unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Consider the graph $G$ whose vertex set is $\mathbb{R}^2$, where two vertices $x, y$ are adjacent if and only if $x - y \in \{\pm v_1, \pm v_2, \pm v_3, \pm v_4\}$. What is the smallest integer $k$ such that $G$ is guaranteed to be $k$-colorable for every possible choice of $V$?

For a given $\lambda>0$, a convex body in $\mathbb R^n$ ($n \geqslant 2$) is called $\lambda$-convex if it is the intersection of a family of closed balls of radius $1/\lambda$. Among all $\lambda$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ with a given fixed inradius $r$ ($0 < r < 1/\lambda$), the mean width is maximized (up to congruence) by a unique body. This maximizing body can be represented as the intersection of exactly $k$ balls of radius $1/\lambda$. What is the integer $k$?

What is the maximum integer dimension $d$ such that every finite geometric simplicial complex $\Delta$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose vertices lie on the moment curve can be extended to a triangulation $T$ of the cyclic polytope $C$ where $\Delta$, $T$, and $C$ all share the same vertex set?

Consider the set of gradient-like diffeomorphisms of the 2-torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ whose induced isomorphism on the first homology group $H_1(\mathbb{T}^2, \mathbb{Z})$ is given by the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} -1 & -1\\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. Into how many stable components does this set of diffeomorphisms decompose?

Let $\overline{\mathcal{H}}_{d,g}(\mu)$ denote the Hurwitz space of fully-marked admissible covers of degree $d$ and genus $g$ with ramification profile $\mu$. What is the smallest integer $d \ge 1$ for which there exist $g$ and $\mu$ such that the first cohomology group $H^1(\overline{\mathcal{H}}_{d,g}(\mu))$ is nonzero?

The chromatic number of the finite projective space $\mathrm{PG}(n-1,q)$, denoted $\chi_q(n)$, is the minimum number of colors needed to color its points so that no line is monochromatic. What is the exact value of $\chi_2(7)$?

Let $X$ be a real normed space, and let $A, B \subseteq X$ be nonempty convex subsets. Define the distance $d(A,B) = \inf\{\|a - b\| : a \in A, b \in B\}$. For any $r > d(A,B)$, define $F_r = B \cap \overline{N}_r(A)$, where $\overline{N}_r(A)$ is the closed $r$-neighborhood of $A$ in $X$. What is the maximum integer $k$ such that for every real normed space $X$ of dimension $k$ and all such convex subsets $A, B \subseteq X$, the Hausdorff distance between $F_{r_1}$ and $F_{r_2}$ is guaranteed to be finite for all $r_1, r_2 > d(A,B)$?

Up to isomorphism, there are exactly 866 smooth projective toric Fano 5-folds. For how many of these does the Hanlon-Hicks-Lazarev resolution of the diagonal yield a full strong exceptional collection of line bundles?

A graph $G$ is $k$-vertex-critical if its chromatic number is $\chi(G)=k$, but $\chi(G')<k$ for every proper induced subgraph $G'$ of $G$. A graph is $\{F_1, F_2\}$-free if neither $F_1$ nor $F_2$ is an induced subgraph of $G$. Up to isomorphism, exactly how many 4-vertex-critical $\{P_7,C_3\}$-free graphs contain an induced $C_7$?

Let $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{k=1}^n \cos(2 \pi a_k \omega)$, where $\omega$ is a uniformly distributed random variable on $[0,1]$. For the integer sequence $a_k = 2^k + 1$, the sixth cumulant of $S_n$ grows asymptotically as $\Theta(n^c)$ as $n \to \infty$. What is the value of the constant $c$?

A compactly supported Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is called a spectral measure if there exists a countable set $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (called a spectrum) such that the set of complex exponentials $\{e^{2\pi i \lambda \cdot x} : \lambda \in \Lambda\}$ forms an orthogonal basis for $L^2(\mu)$. What is the minimum integer $k \ge 1$ for which there exists an arc-length spectral measure supported on the union of $k$ line segments in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that no spectrum of the measure is contained in a single line?

Let $\chi''(G)$ denote the total chromatic number of a graph $G$. Let $C_n(1, 3)$ denote the circulant graph on $n$ vertices, defined by the vertex set $\mathbb{Z}_n$ and edge set $\{ \{i, j\} : i - j \equiv \pm 1, \pm 3 \pmod n \}$. What is the value of the sum $\sum_{n=7}^{17} \chi''(C_n(1, 3))$?

The $\alpha$-Kakutani substitution rule splits the unit interval into two subintervals of lengths $\alpha$ and $1-\alpha$, for a fixed $\alpha \in (0,1)$. A simple inflation-substitution procedure produces tilings of the real line and their associated Delone sets. What is the exact number of distinct values of $\min(\alpha, 1-\alpha)$ for which these sets are uniformly spread (meaning that they are a bounded displacement of a lattice)?

In an acute scalene triangle $ABC$, points $D,E,F$ lie on sides $BC, CA, AB$, respectively, such that $AD \perp BC, BE \perp CA, CF \perp AB$. Altitudes $AD, BE, CF$ meet at orthocenter $H$. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on segment $EF$ such that $AP \perp EF$ and $HQ \perp EF$. Lines $DP$ and $QH$ intersect at point $R$. Compute $HQ/HR$.

For a pair $ A \equal{} (x_1, y_1)$ and $ B \equal{} (x_2, y_2)$ of points on the coordinate plane, let $ d(A,B) \equal{} |x_1 \minus{} x_2| \plus{} |y_1 \minus{} y_2|$. We call a pair $ (A,B)$ of (unordered) points [i]harmonic[/i] if $ 1 < d(A,B) \leq 2$. Determine the maximum number of harmonic pairs among 100 points in the plane.
Draw a $2004 \times 2004$ array of points. What is the largest integer $n$ for which it is possible to draw a convex $n$-gon whose vertices are chosen from the points in the array?
